field_dataset.title: UNH/AMEC cross-flow turbine field sensors · Oct–Dec 2022
field_dataset.physical_scope: A distinct 3.2 m diameter, four-blade field cross-flow turbine, NOT the UNH RM2 1:6 tow-tank rotor or a Nova Scotia location.

families.title: Blade strain
families.scope: Eight foil sensors along one blade

families.title: Electricity
families.scope: Voltsys rectifier power and rotation inferred from generator frequency

field_dataset.original_access: Native source access not qualified. Normal original ADCP README request returned HTTP429; no bypass or bulk acquisition.

studies.title: Blade strain measured with electrical output
studies.finding: The study recorded synchronized blade strain, velocity, thrust, rotor speed and electrical output.
studies.limitation: Abstract-level review. We have not acquired or qualified their original sensor records.

studies.title: Turbulence can materially alter fatigue
studies.finding: Authors report roughly 5× greater fatigue damage at their site versus a typical low-turbulence laboratory case.
studies.limitation: That is their study-specific effect, not a transferable fatigue multiplier.

studies.title: Revolution frequency dominates in another rotor
studies.finding: Their strain-based comparison found revolution frequency dominant over dynamic-flow effects for the studied geometry.
studies.limitation: This does not prove turbulence irrelevant for other devices or make theoretical turns into measured fatigue cycles.

scientific_interpretation: Turbulence and revolution-frequency effects are design-dependent, not contradictory universal rules. Our separate measured inflow, phase, blade stress and metered electricity remain missing.
